title: The Best Software for Architects
summary: The software architecture firms run, by job: BIM and drawings, early design, rendering, review, presentation and practice management, and how the pieces fit.
body_markdown:
Modern architecture firms often run on a software stack, each tool intended for a distinct part of the architectural process: a BIM platform for drawings, a modeler for early design, a real-time renderer, a PDF tool for review, Adobe apps for presentation, and practice-management software. Firms that are trying to adopt high-quality software solutions should understand their options, job by job, and also understand the part that no design tool covers: your firm's own past work.


## Start with the drawings


Choose the BIM platform first, and choose it to best suit your construction documents: that's where your coordination, your consultants and most of your time is focused. Ask yourself five questions:


1. **What do your consultants and clients expect?** If your structural and MEP engineers model in Revit, sharing Revit files directly saves a round of cleanup on every exchange.
2. **What do your machines run?** Revit runs only on Windows. Archicad and Vectorworks run on Mac and Windows.
3. **What files does it trade?** Every tool below either opens your BIM files, plugs into your BIM platform, or trades through IFC, DWG or PDF.
4. **Who already knows it?** The fastest software is the one your staff and your next hires already use.
5. **Can the firm keep one standard in it?** Consistent usage of standard templates, families and details is what makes the fiftieth project faster than the first. Keeping them consistent across projects and offices is the core of[BIM management](https://www.pirros.com/blog/bim-management) .


## The software, by job


Each tool below is described from its maker's own pages. The right choice depends on your BIM platform, your machines and your consultants.


### BIM and construction documents


This is the platform your drawings live in. Firms commit to one and build their templates, families and details around it.


[Revit](https://www.autodesk.com/products/revit/overview) is Autodesk's BIM software to design, coordinate and deliver building projects. It runs only on Windows, and Revit 2027 needs Windows 11; on a Mac, Autodesk's route is a Windows virtual machine in Parallels Desktop. Revit imports, exports and links IFC, Rhino, SketchUp, OBJ and STEP files, and links consultants' DWGs.


[Archicad](https://www.graphisoft.com/en-us/plans-and-products/archicad/) is Graphisoft's BIM software for designing, documenting and collaborating on buildings, on macOS and Windows 11. It trades with Revit mainly through IFC. It can hotlink a Revit model for 3D views and export RVT, though Graphisoft notes the exported elements arrive "frozen and locked".


[Vectorworks Architect](https://www.vectorworks.net/en-US/architect) covers BIM for architecture from concept sketches to construction documents, on Windows 11 and macOS. It imports and exports Revit files (RVT and RFA) as well as IFC.


[AutoCAD](https://www.autodesk.com/products/autocad/overview) is 2D and 3D drafting, and DWG is still how many consultants' drawings and older projects arrive. Its Architecture toolset adds walls, doors, windows and generated plans and sections, but the toolsets are Windows-only; AutoCAD for Mac runs the core program. Revit links or imports DWG files directly.


### Early design and 3D modeling


Early in a project, many firms sketch and test building forms in a quick 3D modeler, then bring the chosen design into their BIM platform to develop the drawings.


[SketchUp](https://sketchup.trimble.com/en) is Trimble's quick 3D modeler for sketching and communicating ideas, on Windows, macOS, iPad and the web. Revit links or imports SketchUp files, and SketchUp's own Revit importer, on Windows and its higher subscription tiers, goes the other way.


[Rhino 8](https://www.rhino3d.com/8/) models complex geometry (NURBS, SubD and meshes) on Windows and macOS, and comes with Grasshopper, a visual editor for parametric design. Revit links or imports Rhino files, and[Rhino.Inside.Revit](https://www.rhino3d.com/inside/revit/1.0/) runs Rhino and Grasshopper inside Revit itself, with more than 300 Revit-aware components.


[Forma Site Design](https://www.autodesk.com/products/forma-site-design/overview) , part of Autodesk Forma, is browser-based site planning, massing and environmental analysis. A proposal goes to Revit as a geolocated native Revit model.


### Rendering and visualization


Real-time renderers let you walk a client through the model while the design is still in development. As you'd imagine, the question of how these tools connect to your BIM platform is very relevant.


[Enscape](https://www.chaos.com/enscape) (Chaos) renders in real time inside Revit 2024–2027 on Windows. Its Mac version works with SketchUp, Rhino, Archicad and Vectorworks, but not Revit.


[Twinmotion](https://www.twinmotion.com/) (Epic Games) is real-time visualization and immersive presentation on Windows and macOS. It stays in sync with Revit 2024 and later through the Datasmith Direct Link built into Revit.


[Lumion](https://lumion.com/compatibility/revit-rendering) makes renders, animations and 360° panoramas on Windows only, with a free LiveSync plugin for Revit.


[D5 Render](https://www.d5render.com/) is real-time photorealistic rendering on Windows with a ray-tracing graphics card. Its D5 Sync plugin sends the Revit model across when you press Sync.


[V-Ray for Revit](https://www.chaos.com/vray/revit) (Chaos) renders photoreal stills without leaving Revit, on Windows. Its requirements page lists Revit 2022–2026, so check Revit 2027 support before you upgrade.


### Review, markup and coordination


Most review still happens on PDFs exported from the BIM platform, with model coordination running alongside.


[Bluebeam Revu](https://www.bluebeam.com/product/) is PDF markup and review built for AEC teams, with live Studio sessions where several people mark up the same set at once. Revu runs on Windows; Bluebeam on web and mobile covers other devices, and Revu for iPad ended in December 2025. A Revit plugin, on the Core, Complete and Max plans, creates PDFs from Revit, including 3D PDFs.


[Adobe Acrobat](https://www.adobe.com/acrobat.html) edits, converts, signs, comments on and compares PDFs, on Windows, macOS, web and mobile. It's a general PDF tool rather than a drawing-review tool, and comparing two revisions needs the Pro version.


[Forma Data Management](https://www.autodesk.com/products/forma-data-management/overview) , the new name for Autodesk Docs, is Autodesk's cloud home for project files: versions, reviews and approvals in one place, viewable in a browser. An Essentials tier comes with stand-alone Revit and AutoCAD, and Revit publishes models to it.


[Navisworks](https://www.autodesk.com/products/navisworks/overview) combines models from Revit and other tools into one model for review and coordination. It reads Revit files directly, Navisworks Manage adds clash detection, and it runs on Windows only.


### Presentation


[Photoshop](https://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) ,[Illustrator](https://www.adobe.com/products/illustrator.html) and[InDesign](https://www.adobe.com/products/indesign.html) are Adobe's image-editing, vector-drawing and page-layout apps, sold through Creative Cloud. Firms use them to touch up renderings, draw diagrams and lay out boards, proposals and portfolios. All three run on Windows and macOS. None connects to Revit, so work comes across as exported images, PDFs or DWGs.


### Practice management


These tools never touch the model. Instead, they connect to the drawings through the hours your team logs against each project, and they're how a principal sees whether a phase is on budget.


[Monograph](https://monograph.com/) is firm-management software built for A&E firms: projects, time, invoicing and firm finances in one place, in a browser, a desktop app, and mobile apps for time and expenses.


[Deltek Ajera](https://www.deltek.com/products/erp/ajera/) combines project management and project accounting for small architecture and engineering firms; its full feature set needs Windows.[Deltek Vantagepoint](https://www.deltek.com/products/erp/vantagepoint/) is Deltek's system for A&E and consulting firms up to large multi-office practices, most of which run it in Deltek's cloud.


[BQE CORE](https://www.bqe.com/) puts CRM, projects, time, billing, accounting and payroll in one web app for architecture, engineering and consulting firms. It runs in any browser on Mac or Windows, with mobile apps for iOS and Android.


### AI in Revit


AI tools now work inside Revit itself.[Mira](https://www.pirros.com/mira) , Pirros's AI agent for Revit, works in your live model and takes the repetitive documentation edits off your week, such as renumbering details or centering room tags, and asks before it changes anything (more below). For the rest of the field, from AI rendering to early-design tools, see our list of[AI tools for Revit](https://www.pirros.com/blog/ai-tools-for-revit) . For AI beyond Revit, see[AI for architecture](https://www.pirros.com/blog/ai-architectural-tools) .


The firm's stack by job, with the BIM platform at the center and how each tool connects to it.


## The same detail gets drawn again


Every tool above creates new files, but none of them make your firm's past work easily searchable and consistent. That's why many firms struggle with the following coordination problems:


- **Details sit in closed projects.** A project ships, its details go to an archive folder, and months later the next team redraws the same condition because finding it takes longer than drawing it.
- **Families multiply.** Nobody can say which of four similar windows is the approved one, so someone builds a fifth, and the near-copies spread across offices.
- **Versions drift.** The right family is stranded in a project saved in an older Revit version, and loading it means an upgrade nobody has time for.
- **Knowledge walks out the door.** What a senior architect solved on a project leaves with them unless the next person can find it.


## Where Pirros and Mira fit


Pirros is the AI project hub for architects and engineers: it makes everything your firm has already drawn findable, trusted and ready to reuse. It's Revit-native and works alongside Autodesk, not in place of it.


- **Every detail, searchable by what's drawn.**[Detail management](https://www.pirros.com/product/detail-management) reads the geometry and annotations inside each detail, so you search by the condition it solves, not a file name. Upload past projects and they're searchable, with duplicates grouped and your firm's vetted version marked.
- **Families you can trust.**[Revit family management](https://www.pirros.com/product/family-management) puts families and details in one place, searchable by dimensions, materials, type names and parameters, with firm-approved families marked "typical".
- **Standards built from real projects.** Pirros suggests the details and families worth making firm standards, shows where the standards have gaps, and ranks approved versions first in search.
- **Inside Revit.** Pirros in Revit puts the same search in a sidebar, so you drag details and families straight into the open model.


Firms see the difference in hours. At[Lake Flato](https://www.pirros.com/customers/how-lake-flato-architects-turned-firm-history-into-everyday-speed-and-quality-with-pirros) , teams "spend 50% less time opening models, upgrading, and previewing Revit content." At[David Baker Architects](https://www.pirros.com/customers/david-baker-architecture-and-pirros-collaborative-content-success) , designers saved an average of 33 hours per project in search and recreation time. More than 400 firms build on Pirros, and they save 15–30+ hours per project.


### Mira handles the repetition; you approve the result


Mira is Pirros's[AI agent for Revit](https://www.pirros.com/mira) , free to download, for Revit 2025, 2026 and 2027 on Windows. It works in your live model. You ask in plain words, it reads the sheet, view or selection first, shows you what it will change and waits for your go-ahead. Its ready-made skills cover jobs Revit leaves you to do one element at a time:


- "Renumber the details on this sheet."
- "Center the room tags in this view."
- "Replace DRAFT with FINAL in every text note."
- "Flip the grid heads on the selected grids."


Afterwards it checks the result and names anything it skipped, and why. Most skills make the whole change as one step, so one Ctrl+Z reverses it.


Mira setting a scope box across a project's floor plans (sped up): it reads every plan first, asks how to handle the 41 that a view template controls, sets 89 of 93 in one step and names the 4 it skipped.


## Build the stack around your drawings


Tools at the edge of the stack come and go, but the BIM platform at the center is the one your firm lives with for years. Choose it for your drawings and your consultants, pick the rest by how well they trade files with it, and keep your firm's details, families and standards where every project can find them. That last piece is what makes each project faster than the one before.


## Check your own stack


Pick the job that occupies the most hours in your week, and check the tool you use for it against the five questions above. If it's the repetitive edits in Revit,[try Mira free](https://www.pirros.com/mira) : it runs in Revit 2025 and later.
